item: The article list's language filter and sort by title read only an index, built once at start-up as a task-manager job (R128)
key_paths: src/database/article_indexes.py; src/database/maintenance.py; src/database/models.py; src/database/session.py; src/api/boot_sequence.py; src/api/jobs.py; src/jobs/background.py; migrations/versions/c3a91f5e7b24_article_list_language_and_title_indexes.py; tests/test_article_indexes.py; tests/test_boot_sequence.py; docs/USER_MANUAL.md
summary: The maintainer answered 34a: both indexes. idx_article_language_published (language, published_at) and idx_article_title_nocase (title COLLATE NOCASE) turn the article list's two remaining slow shapes into index-only reads: the page query of a language filter 1,284 ms to 3 ms and of a sort by title 807 ms to 3 ms cold on a 40,000-article, 2 GB test library, the same answers in the same order. init_db leaves them out (maintenance.DEFERRED_INDEXES); an article-indexes step of the boot sequence, after the check of the data files and before the warm-up, builds what is missing as a task-manager job: one statement each under the write gate, 'index N of M', no Cancel (an opaque statement), the free space measured first (about 400 bytes an article on the database's volume; the temporary-file volume is not measured because the sort is held in memory, about 125 bytes of RAM an article, stated and not gated; a shortfall is a failed row whose keyed detail carries the numbers in both task managers, an unreadable figure is not a refusal), declined when the corpus file is paused as damaged, ANALYZE of just the new indexes afterwards. The title index is declared on the model with collate() so the stamp alignment reads no drift; the language one reads add_index for the one start before the step has built it. OO_ARTICLE_INDEXES=0 leaves them unbuilt. The diagnostics bundle's boot_sequence block carries what the step did. About 190 MB per 1.5 million articles on real titles (130 MB on the synthetic ones). The build on a big store on a slow drive is not measured: the bundle's block will say. The caveat reads anything the app saves waits (every gated write does), the in-app task manager draws the row's detail, a worker thread that cannot start leaves no phantom running job, and a second run carries nothing of the first in its snapshot.
